# Original synthetic chart fixtures

These events were authored only to test timing and validation. They do not contain
a community song chart, audio, Cream material or official Guitar Hero data.

`expected.json` contains hand-calculated values, not snapshots generated by the
importer. Additional invalid/edge cases are constructed in the Python tests.

- `constant.chart`: 100 ticks/quarter note and 120 BPM. One beat is 500000 us.
  Tick 100 is 500000 us; tick 300 is 1500000 us. A 200-tick sustain lasts 1000000 us.
  The two tick-100 notes form a source-order chord.
- `tempo_changes.chart`: resolution 192, Offset +0.25 s. From tick 0 to 384,
  two beats at 120 BPM take 1 s. Tick 384 to 576 is one beat at 60 BPM, taking
  another 1 s. Tick 576 to 768 is one beat at 240 BPM, taking .25 s.
  Thus ticks 192/384/576/768 are .75/1.25/2.25/2.50 s at the audio origin.
  A sustain from 192 to 768 lasts .5 + 1 + .25 = 1.75 s, not .5 × 3 = 1.5 s.
  Four distinct difficulty tracks, open notes, HOPO/tap markers, a phrase, global
  text and an impossible Hard Left+Right chord exercise prepared-feature reports.

The tests independently check alternate resolutions, 100 alternating tempo
segments (exact total 175000000/9 us), offsets, boundaries, numeric limits and
malformed input. They do not merely compare output to the same converter's prior
output. Generated C++ declarations are checked on desktop and GBA compilers when
available; absence of the GBA compiler is an explicit skipped test.
